verdict.rationale: Blaxel sandboxes run as separate cloud environments. Its outbound proxy can inject secrets into headers and bodies via MITM, so credentials need not live inside the sandbox where agent code could read them. Per-domain firewalls and allowlists limit exfiltration, and a non-root user mode keeps executed code unprivileged while the sandbox API retains its privileges. Missing for 10: an explicit doc statement that proxy-injected secrets are never visible to in-sandbox code, detail on the isolation boundary (VM/microVM) between the sandbox and host infrastructure, and independent or hands-on corroboration.
